bioghist.head: Historical Information
bioghist.p: The Department of Conservation and Recreation has a long history, beginning in 1926 with the establishment of the State Commission on Conservation and Development. The State Commission on Conservation and Development consolidated the powers and duties of the Water Power and Development Commission, the State Geological Commission, the State Geological Survey, the State Geologist, the State Forester, and the Division of Parks. In 1927, the Division of Advertising and Publicity was added, followed by the Bureau of History and Archaeology in 1928. In 1936, the State Commission on Conservation and Development gained custody, control and supervision of the World War I memorial, the Carillon in Richmond's Byrd Park, from the Virginia War Memorial Commission, which was then abolished.

In 1938, the State Commission on Conservation and Development became the Virginia Conservation Commission, with no change in duty. The name of the department was changed once again in 1948, this time to the Department of Conservation and Development. In 1958, the Department of Conservation and Development was renamed the Department of Conservation and Economic Development, and three new divisions were added: the Division of Industrial Development, the Division of Mineral Resources, and the Division of Public Relations and Advertising. In 1984, the Dept. of Conservation and Development changed its name to the Dept. of Conservation and Historic Resources, with a restructuring of the divisions of the Department.

The Department of Conservation and Recreation was created in 1989 by an act of the General Assembly. Charged with the mission to "conserve, protect, enhance and advocate the wise use of the Commonwealth's unique natural, historic, recreational, scenic and cultural resources," the Department of Conservation and Recreation is comprised of the following divisions: State Parks; Soil and Water Conservation; Natural Heritage Program; Recreational Planning; and Dam Safety. With this restructuring, the Virginia Historic Landmarks Commission became the Dept. of Historic Resources.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: Correspondence and subject files of the Virginia Dept. of Conservation and Development, 1927-1956, include records related to the Cumberland Gap National Historical Park, Richmond National Battlefield Park, Shenandoah National Park, Virginia Citizens' Carillon Committee, and the Water Supply and Power Division, as well as subject files related to histioric properties. Types of records include abstracts of title, condemnation proceedings, correspondence, deeds, maps, minutes and reports.

did.unittitle: Cumberland Gap National Historical Park records, 1945-1954.

scopecontent.p: Cumberland Gap National Historical Park records, 1945-1954, include abstracts of title, condemenation proceedings and surveys. Abstracts of title include correspondence, abstractor notes, deed transcripts, plats, tract descriptions, and various affidavits and certificates. Cumberland Gap National Historical Park was authorized by Congress on June 11, 1940, developed, and dedicated in July 1959. The park is comprised on land in Bell and Harlan Counties, KY; Claiborne County, TN; and Lee County, VA. These records document the process of the Commonwealth of Virginia acquiring land in Lee County to be deeded to the federal government for the creation on the national park.

did.unittitle: Alphabetical list of tracts of land surveyed, 1951.

scopecontent.p: Richmond Battlefield Park records, 1927-1943, include certificates of title, deeds, maps and reports. Richmond Battlefields Park Corporation was formed in 1927 to raise money to purchase and preserve Civil War battlefield sites in the Richmond, Va. area. The lands were transferred to the Virginia State Conservation and Development Commission in 1932 for the creation of a state park, but the Commission was unable to obtain the needed funds for the development and maintenance of the park, so the lands were deeded to the federal government 1934-1936 for the creation of the Richmond National Battlefields Park. These records includes Deeds, 1927-1932, to the Richmond Battlefields Park Corporation; Deeds, 1932, to the Virginia State Conservation and Development Commission; List and Maps of properties to be conveyed, 1927-1935; Narrative Reports, 1934; and Certificates of Title, 1939.

scopecontent.p: Shenandoah National Park records, 1929-1936, include correspondence and deeds to the State Commission on Conservation and Development, and copies of deeds from the Commission to the federal government. An Act of General Assembly March 22, 1928 (National Park Act, Acts 1928, Chap 371, p. 983) includes provisions for the State Commission on Conservation and Development to acquire land in in the Blue Ridge Mountains (Albemarle County, Augusta County, Greene County, Madison County, Page County Rappahannock County, and Rockingham County, Virginia) through condemnation proceedings to be sold to the federal government for the establishment of a public park to be know as the Shenandoah National Park.

Water Supply and Power Division records, 1931-1944.

scopecontent.p: Water Resources and Power Division records, 1931-1944, contain correspondence and investigation files. Includes Correspondence of the Chairman of the State Commission on Conservation and Development, as well as investigation records related to the alleged improper use of state and federal funds by J.J. Dirzulaitis, District Engineer, Geological Survey; and Chief Engineer, Water Resources and Power Division; and investigation records related to a water resources inquiry into water supply development and springs in Shenandoah National Park..

scopecontent.p: Virginia Citizens' Carillon Committee records, 1927-1935, include correspondence, articles of agreement, clippings, financial records, lists and minutes. The Virginia Citizens' Carillon Committee was formed in 1926 to advocate for a Virginia War Memorial Carillon to the the dead of World War I and to raise money via public subscription to purchase bronze bells for the tower. The majority of the correspondence is related to subscriptions and other financial matters, but also includes a significant amount of correspondence with John Taylor and Co. Bell Founders and Bell Hangers of Loughborough, England, related to the purchase and importation of bronze bells for the tower. The Virginia War Memorial Carillon was dedicated on October 15, 1932 and custody was transferred to Virginia State Commission on Conservation and Development between 1936-1939.
